title: To Go Far, Go Together: Diverse Preferences Induce a Curriculum for Reward Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2608.18770v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Learning a reward model from human feedback and optimizing a policy against it is one approach to aligning AI systems with individual users. From a fairness perspective, existing work improves such alignment by developing data-efficient and accurate reward models that capture minority preferences despite scarce data. We push this line of inquiry one step further and argue that data-efficient and accurate per-user reward models are not sufficient: users whose reward models are difficult to \textit{optimize} at the policy level can become a new underserved group. We start from the observation that one user's reward model can be easy to optimize from the initial policy while another's is not. We argue that, given a sufficiently diverse user population, a curriculum naturally emerges between easy- and hard-to-optimize reward models. translated_title: 欲行远，须同行：多样化的偏好催生奖励优化的课程学习
translated_abstract: 摘要：从人类反馈中学习奖励模型并据此优化策略，是将AI系统与个体用户对齐的一种方法。从公平性角度出发，现有工作通过开发数据高效且准确的奖励模型来改进这种对齐，即使数据稀缺也能捕捉少数群体的偏好。我们将这一研究方向推进了一步，并认为数据高效且准确的逐用户奖励模型并不足够：那些在策略层面难以优化的用户奖励模型可能成为新的服务不足群体。我们从观察出发，发现从初始策略看，一个用户的奖励模型可能易于优化，而另一个用户的则不然。我们认为，在用户群体足够多样化的前提下，易于优化和难以优化的奖励模型之间自然会产生一种课程学习模式。基于这一见解，我们提出了CurriPO，它构建了一个树状结构的课程学习框架，以适应多样化的用户需求。
tldr: 本文提出CurriPO方法，通过构建树状课程学习框架，利用用户偏好多样性自然形成的优化难度差异，确保所有用户（包括难以优化的群体）在奖励优化中得到公平对待。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes CurriPO, which leverages the natural curriculum arising from diverse user preferences via a tree-structured framework, ensuring fair treatment for all users, including those with hard-to-optimize reward models.
